description: [S7.11] On the device-less path the engine subclasses its window before the device probe (SetWindowLongA(window, GWL_WNDPROC, soundWindowSubclassProc) in the shadow's command lines, before DSOUND #2) and initSound's failure path (music-device open returns 3, freeSoundLib) makes no SetWindowLongA that restores the previous procedure. In the original freeSoundLib FreeLibrary's sound.dll, so the game window's procedure would then point into an unloaded module; the original runs on (CLAUDE.md, no-audio-output paragraph), and why is not measured. The shadow's window is a token, so the app is unaffected.
path to resolution: on the original without a device: GetWindowLongA(game window, GWL_WNDPROC) after initSound and the module that holds it (a Frida probe in a device-less boot)

description: [S7.11] Focus loss is DirectSound's own rule, not engine code: the engine makes its primary buffer with flags 0x1, its mixer stream buffer with 0x10088 (GETCURRENTPOSITION2, CTRLVOLUME, LOCSOFTWARE) and its static buffers with 0x100e0 (GETCURRENTPOSITION2, CTRLVOLUME, CTRLPAN, CTRLFREQUENCY), none with DSBCAPS_GLOBALFOCUS (0x8000) or DSBCAPS_STICKYFOCUS (0x4000), and calls SetCooperativeLevel(window, 2 = DSSCL_PRIORITY) (DsSink describe and the shadow's command lines, log/roadmap/S7/11_focus_describe.txt). The app's sink passes the same flags (only the 3D / hardware / defer bits dropped) and its own window, so DirectSound applies the same muting when the window loses focus. Not observed on a device (none on LIVING-PC). --live-trace has no window and passes the desktop window.
path to resolution: with a device: play a static-buffer sound, move the focus to another window, check the buffer is inaudible (loopback capture) while GetStatus still reports PLAYING, in the original and the app

description: [S7.11] Shutdown counts. The audio thread leaves no thread id (Toolhelp32; the bare count moves with the system's thread-pool workers, 4 -> 2 in one cycle) and no handle in Capture / Model / forced-no-device runs (4 start .. stop cycles each, x64 and Win32; the app's handle delta equals an audio-free reference's over the same span). A process's first real DirectSoundCreate (failing here: DSERR_NODRIVER) leaves 18 handles (20 in the app), constant over later cycles: the system's audio DLLs stay loaded. The real-device path (buffers and IDirectSound released, dsound's own threads) was not counted: no device.
path to resolution: run test_app_audio's shutdown test in dsound mode on a PC with an output device

description: [S7.11] Pause: the pause key (code 0x50, case 0x47 of the byte table 0x0042191c) runs `xor [0x0059e7b8], 4` at 0x0041d020 and jumps to the dispatch's end (0x0041d027): no sound call; P5 (0x004175f2) skips the tick while bit 2 is set, so the sim's tick-made requests stop and the UI ones continue; the engine's timer is independent of g_flags, so sounds already playing play out. The shadow copies exactly the sim's requests, so nothing is ported. No corpus trace pauses (time_model.md: no paused frame), so this is argued from the code, not judged on a run.
path to resolution: a scenario with the pause key held over a sound (cov_* family) recorded with the original and run through the app with --audio capture

description: [S7.11] Long session (U-1692): see 11_notes.md section 4 for the measured heap and tick cost over course_season_6y (50,923 frames). The arena reuses a freed block only for an allocation of its exact rounded size, so fragmentation grows with the variety of large sound files played; the measured run stayed in the numbers there. A session that plays every music file was not measured.
path to resolution: an app session that plays each of the install's music files in turn, reading heap_peak_arena_bytes
